analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Week ahead is led by September US CPI on Wednesday and PPI on Thursday, the last inflation data before the Fed's October 28 meeting. Retail sales (Thursday) and industrial production (Friday) give the activity read.

DB economists expect headline September CPI at +0.57% MoM (August +0.40%), about 3.64% YoY, driven by a 9.6% seasonally adjusted jump in motor fuel. They expect core CPI at +0.16% MoM (August +0.29%), taking the annual rate down a couple of basis points to 2.39%.

DB's ex-ante estimate for core PCE (released October 29, the day after the FOMC) is about +0.21% MoM, with the annual rate roughly steady at 3.0%. If data land near these forecasts, DB thinks the Fed can stay on hold on October 28 and wait for more information before December.
Chair Warsh's fireside chat with IMF Managing Director Georgieva on Thursday evening is the last Fed appearance before the communications blackout.

DB US equity strategists expect Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth of a record 34% YoY versus consensus at 27%, arguing consensus embeds too much slowdown. DB European strategists expect 25% Q3 earnings growth, 5pp above consensus.

Trump announced a Russia/Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' on Sunday. Russia has not publicly confirmed it, and Zelenskyy said Russia struck a Kharkiv thermal power plant and other energy infrastructure afterward, so it looks like an untested US proposal.

A temporary US sanctions waiver would let about 13.5 million barrels of Russian diesel into global markets this month, potentially including the first US imports since March 2022. Returning Russian barrels would be bearish for diesel cracks.

Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport was hit again Sunday after repeated attacks over the past week (Saturday's attack killed 12 and wounded more than 300). Houthi gains near Bab el-Mandeb and the possibility of US strikes leave an upside tail risk for oil and shipping costs, alongside continuing Strait of Hormuz disruption.

Last week the 10yr Treasury yield fell 3.3bps to 5.24% after hitting 5.36% intraday on Wednesday, the highest since 2002. The Franco-German 2yr spread tightened 14.6bps to 52bps and the 10yr spread tightened 3.7bps to 137bps as Eurozone financial stress moderated.
The S&P 500 hit a record on Wednesday and gained 1.15% on the week. The STOXX 600 was flat (+0.03%), and the CAC 40 fell 1.19%, its 8th weekly decline in 9. STOXX Banks fell 2.46%.
Brent rose 2.42% last week to $104.72/bbl and European natural gas rose 8.93% to €81.40/MWh, its highest weekly close since 2022. Gold rose 1.28% and copper 2.18%.
Big US banks report Tuesday (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Citigroup) and Wednesday (Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, BlackRock). ASML (Wednesday) and TSMC (Thursday) give a read on AI capex.
earnings_insights: DB US equity strategists expect Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 34% YoY (record) versus consensus of 27%, and see scope for another quarter of above-average beats.
DB European equity strategists expect Q3 earnings growth of 25%, 5pp above consensus.

A fragile or failed Russia/Ukraine energy ceasefire and strains between Washington and Kyiv.
Continued European financial stress (France, European banks) despite last week's moderation.

geopolitical: Trump announced an immediate Russia/Ukraine 'energy ceasefire'. Russia has not publicly confirmed it and Zelenskyy said Russia struck Kharkiv energy infrastructure afterward.

US temporary sanctions waiver for about 13.5 million barrels of Russian diesel, linked to the ceasefire. Zelenskyy criticised it, and Reuters reported Washington threatened to cut intelligence sharing and weapons procurement support unless Kyiv halted refinery strikes.

Repeated attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, attributed to the Houthis. Saudi Arabia has intensified air strikes in Yemen and Trump said the US 'may' join strikes against the Houthis.
Houthi gains near Bab el-Mandeb are being countered by Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces. Iran denied directing the Houthis and its foreign minister urged diplomacy with Saudi Arabia.
Continuing Strait of Hormuz disruption and a lack of clear progress between the US and Iran.
